classification.difficultyReason: Read cosine values from the supplied graph, then reverse the lookup by finding both intersections at each given cosine value and estimating their angles.

content.prompt: This graph shows $\cos\theta$. Use it to estimate the following to 2 d.p.

spec.description: Editable cosine graph with a 10-degree by 0.1 fine grid, stronger major lines, ticks, axis arrows and a continuing curve arrow. Increased physical width supports readable graph labels.
spec.mathematics: y=cos(theta), with theta measured in degrees; displayed grid covers 0 to 360 and -1 to 1. Horizontal labels are 90, 180, 270 and 360; vertical labels are -1, -0.5, 0.5 and 1.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is visible in every edition; no answer guides are included.

answer.worked: From $35^{\circ}$ on the horizontal axis, read vertically to the curve and then horizontally to the vertical axis: $\cos35^{\circ}\approx0.82$.
From $190^{\circ}$ on the horizontal axis, read vertically to the curve and then horizontally to the vertical axis: $\cos190^{\circ}\approx-0.98$.
From $330^{\circ}$ on the horizontal axis, read vertically to the curve and then horizontally to the vertical axis: $\cos330^{\circ}\approx0.87$.
From $140^{\circ}$ on the horizontal axis, read vertically to the curve and then horizontally to the vertical axis: $\cos140^{\circ}\approx-0.77$.

children.prompt: Use the same graph as in Q1 to estimate the $\underline{\textbf{values}}$ of $\theta$ between $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ for the following. Give estimates to the nearest degree.

answer.worked: The horizontal line at $0.8$ meets the cosine curve twice. Reading the corresponding angles gives $\theta\approx37^\circ$ or $323^\circ$.
The horizontal line at $0.6$ meets the cosine curve twice. Reading the corresponding angles gives $\theta\approx53^\circ$ or $307^\circ$.
The cosine curve crosses the horizontal axis at $90^\circ$ and $270^\circ$, so these are the two solutions.
The horizontal line at $-0.4$ meets the cosine curve twice. Reading the corresponding angles gives $\theta\approx114^\circ$ or $246^\circ$.
